$description: Wingtip Maps' design language, the one source for the web, iOS and Android (W3C Design Tokens format: $value, $type, $description; Wingtip's per-platform mappings under $extensions["app.wingtipmaps"]). scripts/build/design-tokens.sh generates apps/web/src/styles/tokens.css, apps/web/src/lib/tokens.ts, apps/ios/Wingtip/Design/Generated/Tokens.swift and apps/android/app/src/main/kotlin/app/wingtipmaps/android/design/generated/Tokens.kt from it; CI regenerates them and fails on a difference. Change a value here, never in a generated file.

chart.$description: The colours drawn on the chart. They are the chart's own, so they stay the same at night, as the sectional under them does.

course.$description: The course line's magenta, as an FAA chart draws a course: the route, a hold's racetrack, a top of climb's tag. The same at night.

route-green.$description: The green either side of a selected course, as ForeFlight cases its magenta (the owner's screenshot, 2026-11-08): no airspace, airway or field on the sectional is drawn in it.

route-green-night.$description: The route's green a shade deeper over the dimmed chart, so it does not glare.

route-edge.$description: The thin edge round the course's magenta by day (white at 35% over the dimmed chart).

waypoint.$description: A VFR waypoint's magenta, the sectional's.

map-blue.$description: iOS's systemBlue, the blue Maps draws its own marks in: the position dot, a point held on the chart, a procedure's Direct to. Not the tint, which is a step deeper for words on white.

towered.$description: The sectional's blue: "Airports having control towers are shown in blue, all others in magenta" (FAA Aeronautical Chart User's Guide, VFR Terms and Symbols, Airports). Also VORs.

untowered.$description: The sectional's magenta for a field with no tower (Chart User's Guide, Airports).

field-unknown.$description: A field whose tower is not known yet.

airspace-blue.$description: Class B (solid) and D (dashed) lines in ForeFlight's brighter blue, as the sectional codes them (Chart User's Guide, Airspace). Also a fix's blue.

airspace-magenta.$description: Class C (solid) and E (dashed, faded) lines in ForeFlight's brighter magenta (Chart User's Guide, Airspace). Also a MOA's line.

airspace-tab.$description: The dark tab an airspace's altitudes sit in, at 90%.

nexrad-1.$description: FIS-B NEXRAD's levels (DO-358B; 0 is none) drawn from light green through yellow and red to magenta, as radar pictures run from the faintest returns to the strongest. Level 1, the faintest.

special-use.$description: Prohibited, restricted, warning and alert areas (special-use airspace, FAA Order JO 7400.10): the orange-brown hatch.

fix-ink.$description: A fix's and a runway number's dark ink.

vfr-green.$description: A VFR reporting point's green on the map.

runway-hard.$description: A paved runway's surface (ForeFlight's dark grey over its street map).

runway-soft.$description: A runway that is not hard: turf, grass, dirt, gravel.

procedure.$description: A procedure's indigo on the map and its pill.

tfr.$description: A temporary flight restriction's red (14 CFR 91.137 to 91.145).

emergency.$description: The emergency assistant's line to the field picked: the system red a pilot reads as now.

casing.$description: The white a mark, a line or a label is cased and haloed in so it reads over any part of the chart, and the paper under a diagram.

tag.$description: The dark ground a label sits on over the chart: an airport's name halo, a field's tag on the route, a traffic label, an airspace's chip.

shade.$description: The dark ring round a checkpoint's halo and the edge of a map control, at about half strength.

warning.$description: Something in the way on the chart and in the side view: terrain or an obstacle at or above the airplane, a track off the route (iOS's accessible system red).

caution.$description: The side view's and the pilot's-eye view's amber: ground within the engine's caution band below the airplane.

terrain.$description: The ground in a profile, the nav log's and the side view's.

selected.$description: The ring round the field whose card is open and round a point picked on the chart: the brand's Taxiway Yellow (the owner, 2026-11-09), cased in chart.casing and an edge of chart.shade, as a picked point's ring, so it holds over the sectional's pale greens and its towns' yellow.

course-chip.$description: The course's magenta a step darker, for a chip with white words on it (6:1; the course's own is 3.8:1): a way's name and time on its line.

pattern.$description: A traffic pattern's legs and arrows, in teal so they stand apart from the route's magenta (ForeFlight draws its in a cyan).

pattern-label.$description: A pattern leg's name ground, a step darker: white words on it 5.2:1, where the line's teal is 3.95:1 (WCAG 1.4.3).

final-approach.$description: An approach's final segment, its final approach fix to its missed approach point, over its plate on the map: the cyan ForeFlight marks it in (the owner's screenshot, 2026-11-11), apart from the procedure's indigo and the course's magenta. A chart colour, so the same in every look and at night.

sky.$description: The sky over the tilted 3D map by day, the chart's pale blue (features/plan/map/terrain/SkyGl).

sky-horizon.$description: The sky's pale band at the horizon by day, and the haze the far ground fades into.

sky-night.$description: The 3D map's sky over the dimmed chart at night: dark, so it does not glare over a chart dimmed for the cockpit.

sky-horizon-night.$description: The horizon's band and the far ground's haze at night, a step lighter than the night sky so the horizon still reads.

centreline.$description: A runway's extended centreline on the ground in the 3D view, white over the chart and the satellite imagery alike, as a runway's own centreline is painted.

glidepath.$description: The glidepath in the air to a runway's threshold in the 3D view: the final approach segment's cyan, as it is the same descent.

airspace-floor-low.$description: What a 3D airspace volume's class ink is mixed toward the lower its floor (features/plan/map/terrain/airspaceShelves): a surface area darkest, so a Class B's shelves step up in shade as they do in altitude.

airspace-floor-high.$description: And toward the higher its floor: the highest shelf lightest.

obstacle.$description: An obstacle under 1,000 ft AGL in the 3D view; a taller one is in the warning red.

map-ground.$description: The map's ground before its first tiles are drawn, by day (Tailwind slate-100, as it was).

badge.$description: A row's badge by what the row is about, one colour per kind on every card and console row, as iOS's Settings leads every row with one; never a flight category's colour, so a badge is not read as weather.

fuel.$description: A stop's services: the fuel, a car, food, a bed.

stop-fuel.$description: The Stops sheet's kinds, one colour each for a pill, a line, a Find Nearby tile and the map's pin (the owner's picks on the Stops canvas, 2026-10-27): fuel.

home.$description: Home's mark, a Favorite tile's and a row's (Tailwind teal-600, as it was drawn).

airplane.$description: An airplane's own mark on a tile or a row: its profile's, a Favorite's (Tailwind sky-600, as it was drawn).

air.$description: A tracked airplane's "In the air" badge on its card, white on it (Tailwind teal-700, as it was drawn).

status-active.$description: StatusBadge's fills, one per status a pilot scans for (the owner, 2026-11-14: "Use badges where we can for example tfr active etc."), each under white words at 4.5:1 or more in both schemes (WCAG 1.4.3; looksContrast.test.ts): in force now, the hazard's red (6.6:1).

status-later.$description: In force later, not yet: amber-700 (5.0:1).

status-cold.$description: Scheduled but not in use now (a cold special-use area): grey-500 (4.8:1).

status-closed.$description: A field or runway NASR or a NOTAM closes (decision 0043): red-800 (8.3:1), a step past Active's so the two are told apart.

status-out-of-service.$description: A navaid or a service out of service: orange-800 (7.3:1).

status-private.$description: A private-use field (NASR's use PR): slate-600 (7.6:1).

status-military.$description: A military field (NASR's ownership MA, MN, MR, CG): lime-700, an olive drab (5.0:1).

status-emergency.$description: An emergency's squawk on a tracked airplane (AIM 6-2-2): the light gun's red, red-600 (4.8:1).

status-ground.$description: A tracked airplane on the ground: iOS's dark grey, zinc-600 (7.7:1).

weather.$description: A weather area or a PIREP on the map by what it warns of, as aviationweather.gov's own map tells them apart: convective red-orange, icing blue, turbulence amber, IFR and mountains obscured violet and stone, the winds teal.

ash.$description: Volcanic ash, and a PIREP of nothing in particular.

other.$description: An area whose hazard has no colour of its own.

flow-streak.$description: The flow layer's wind streaks (features/weather-flow), white with a breath of blue as Apple Weather's wind map draws them, the owner's screenshot (2026-11-11).

flow-wind-calm.$description: The wind's field, one hue deepening with speed, the map tinted rather than a rainbow (Apple Weather's wind map): calm.

flow-rain-light.$description: Precipitation by intensity, blue to violet to magenta to yellow (Apple Weather's precipitation map): light.

flow-cloud.$description: Cloud cover, the same grey-white thicker with cover.

flow-ceiling-lifr.$description: The ceiling, by AIM 7-1-7's categories in the airport marks' own colours (category.lifr and the rest), strongest where it is lowest: under 500 ft.

flow-ceiling-vfr.$description: Over 3,000 ft, fading to clear where there is none.

flow-cape-weak.$description: Thunderstorm energy, surface CAPE, by the NWS's categories, yellow through orange and red to magenta as the SPC's mesoanalysis draws it: weak, from a few hundred J/kg.

flow-temp-frigid.$description: The 2 m temperature, violet through blue, teal, green and yellow to red (Apple Weather's temperature map): -30 C.

flow-vis-low.$description: Visibility, a slate veil that clears as it rises: the least.

flow-vis-high.$description: Ten miles, where the veil has gone.

flow-icing-trace.$description: AWC's icing severity (IFI), pale to deep blue as aviationweather.gov's Icing map shades it: trace.

flow-turb-light.$description: AWC's turbulence (GTG, EDR), green to amber to red to magenta as its Turbulence map shades it: light.

flow-frz-low.$description: The freezing level, ft MSL, blue where it is low (at the surface) to warm where it is high: the surface.

flow-tops-low.$description: AWC's cloud tops, ft MSL, grey-white deepening to slate as they rise: low tops.

flow-hatch.$description: The thin diagonal lines over where the layer has no data, as Apple Weather hatches it.

score.$description: How good a checkpoint is: one ochre hue, pale to dark, more ink for a better landmark (the planner's scores and the training workspace's ratings, one scale). Not green-to-red, so no step is read as a flight category; each is 13.8 OKLab units and more from every category's colour, the palest 2.4:1 on the markers' white casing.

signal.$description: The tower's light gun signals (14 CFR 91.125; AIM 4-3-13), as the drill shows them.

category.$description: The FAA's flight categories (AIM 7-1-7, Categorical Outlooks), in the colours a pilot already reads them in: green good, blue marginal, red instrument, magenta worse. Grey where the field filed no report, which is unknown, not fine.

lifr.$description: The pip and the mark on the map.

lifr-chip.$description: LIFR as a chip's fill under white words: #a371f7 is 3.35:1 under white, this 6.4:1 (WCAG 1.4.3; the UI audit, 2026-11-09).

brand.$description: Wingtip's mark (docs/brand): the ownship chevron in navy in a sectional's dashed magenta ring.

mark-ring.$description: Airspace Magenta, the ring round the mark.

launch.$description: The launch screen's ground by day (iOS UILaunchScreen, Android's splash, the installed web app's): the app's own first screen's background, as Apple asks a launch screen to be, the mark on it (scripts/build/app-icons.sh).

launch-night.$description: The launch screen's ground at night: the night theme's navy, the mark lit on it.

chart-land.$description: The sectional's lowland green the app icon is drawn on (docs/brand/appicon.svg): the store art's and the small icon's ground.

flown.$description: What is flown already, on the strip's ribbon.

theme.$description: The app's surfaces, words and states in each scheme. Names are the web's custom properties; the phones take them in their own idiom (iOS's system colours for its grounds; Material roles on Android).

airspace-blue-text.$description: A side view's airspace name in the sectional's blue.

course.$description: The course's magenta off the map: the nav log's tags, FPL's route line.

primary.$description: A filled button's fill, white words on it: iOS's blue a step deeper (#0066CC), 5.6:1 on white where #007AFF is 4:1.

tint.$description: The words and glyphs of everything tappable that is not a filled button. Plain text is never in it.

tint-shade.$description: The tint on the sheet's shade under its glass, a step deeper to keep 4.5:1.

sheet.$description: The sheet's own opaque ground: iOS's grouped grey, white cards on it.

airspace-blue-ink.$description: The words of a dashed Class D pill, 4.5:1 on its wash.

airspace-magenta-ink.$description: The words of a dashed Class E pill.

caution.$description: Caution, the one amber (Tailwind amber-700 a step deeper): words and marks. 4.6:1 on Chart ink's muted, where amber-700 was 4.1:1 (looksContrast.test.ts, 2026-11-09).

go.$description: Go, the one green, for marks (green-600 a step deeper): 3.2:1 on Chart ink's muted, a mark's 3:1 (WCAG 1.4.11), where green-600 was 2.6:1 (looksContrast.test.ts, 2026-11-09).

go-ink.$description: Go's words (green-800): green-700 was 4.43:1 on the Brief's glass.

muted-foreground-shade.$description: Grey words on the sheet's shade under its glass, a step deeper to keep 4.5:1, as the tint's shade is.

muted-foreground.$description: Grey words, 4.5:1 and more on the sheet's #f2f2f7 as on white: 0.556 was 4.25:1 on the sheet (the UI audit, 2026-11-09).

destructive.$description: Red-600 a step deeper: set as words (text-destructive) it reads 4.6:1 on Chart ink's muted and 5:1 on the sheet, where red-600 was 3.9 and 4.3:1 (looksContrast.test.ts, 2026-11-09).

destructive-ink.$description: Red words on a destructive button's pale red, 5.4:1 (red-700).

input.$description: A field's edge, 3:1 on the background (WCAG 1.4.11).

ring.$description: The focus ring, in the tint as everything tappable is (5.6:1 on white; a look's own tint follows it).

dark.$description: Night: the cockpit's navy (the owner's dark palette, 2026-10-26): #0B1422 ground, #17283A surface. Every word on every surface 4.5:1 and more (WCAG 1.4.3); apps/web/src/lib/contrast.test.ts holds it to that.

popover.$description: A step above the card, so a menu opened over one stands off it.

primary.$description: A fill near-white words read on at 4.7:1.

tint.$description: Wingtip blue at night, for words and glyphs on the navy: 6:1 on the card (the owner, 2026-11-09).

destructive.$description: A shade lighter than the day's red: 4.9:1 on the muted.

sunlight.$description: A screen held up in a sunlit cockpit: no glass, solid white, black words and a deep blue tint (the owner's canvas, 2026-11-03). Wins over light, dark and every look.

primary.$description: Wingtip blue in sunlight, a step deeper for the solid white (the owner, 2026-11-09).

caution.$description: Sunlight's states are the day's, a step deeper, at night too: the night's pale amber, green and red were 1.5 to 2.5:1 on sunlight's white (the token contrast test, apps/web/src/lib/looksContrast.test.ts, 2026-11-09). 5.4:1 on the muted.

destructive.$description: 5.6:1 on the muted; white on it 6.5:1.

look.$description: The looks. Wingtip, the brand's own blue (#0066CC by day, #57A8FF at night, #0047A0 in sunlight), is the default on every app (the owner, 2026-11-09) and is the theme itself, so it names nothing here. Glass Cockpit and Chart ink, the two kept on 2026-11-04, stay as choices, and Native, the platform's own (2026-11-10); each changes only what it names, over the theme.

primary.$description: The cockpit's cyan, deepened to read on white (5.6:1).
A deep teal for fills under white words (5.3:1).

tint.$description: The panel's cyan for words (8.4:1 on the card).

ink.$description: Chart ink: the app in the FAA sectional's own ink. A paper ground under white cards with no edge; the chart's magenta for the course and an ident at a head, its brown for a checkpoint, its green for a field. The tint stays the app's blue by day: the canvas's #0a84ff reads 3.7:1 on white.

ink-magenta.$description: The course and an ident at a head; 5.0:1 on the paper.

ink-brown.$description: A checkpoint's mark, by day and at night (it sits on the chart); 5.3:1 on the paper.

ink-field.$description: A field's green, by day and at night; 4.8:1 on the paper.

muted-foreground.$description: 7.9:1 on a card, 7.0:1 on the paper.

border.$description: The paper a shade deeper: a hairline between a list's rows.

primary.$description: A light teal for what can be tapped, as words (10.4:1 on the ground) and as a fill under the ground's own dark words.

ink-magenta.$description: A lighter magenta, 5.9:1 on a card.

native.$description: Native: each platform as it comes out of the box (the owner, 2026-11-10: "Native means how they come out of the box, look and behavior wise"), untouched by Wingtip. On the phones (`all`) every surface, word and tint is the system's own colour by reference (color.system), what an untinted SwiftUI view or a stock MaterialTheme draws, light or dark as the device is. On the web (`web`) it is shadcn's stock theme for the base-vega style and the neutral base colour (components.json), the CSS variables `shadcn init` writes, as they are: no contrast adjustment of ours, so where a stock default is under WCAG's line it is reported, not changed (looksContrast.test.ts). What it does not name stays the theme's on purpose: the caution, go and destructive states, the course and the chart's colours, the flight categories and the mark are aviation's, not a component's chrome, the same in every look.

web.$description: shadcn's stock CSS variables, base-vega on neutral (ui.shadcn.com/docs/theming, the :root and .dark blocks), as written; the four roles after them are Wingtip's own names, each set to the stock role a stock component draws it in.

sheet.$description: The app's sheet is shadcn's Drawer, whose ground is bg-background.

tint.$description: What the app tints, in shadcn's own link and ghost colour: its primary, near black by day and near white at night. shadcn has no blue.

sheet.$description: The app's sheet is shadcn's Drawer, whose ground is bg-background.

tint.$description: What the app tints, in shadcn's own link and ghost colour: its primary, near black by day and near white at night. shadcn has no blue.

primary.$description: A filled button in the system's link blue, not the web's AccentColor: Safari's is iOS's #007AFF, 4.0:1 under white words, under WCAG 1.4.3's 4.5:1, and a Mac's may be yellow. AccentColor is the ring's and the form controls' (accent-color: auto).

tint.$description: Words and glyphs of what can be tapped.

ring.$description: The focus ring, a mark (3:1, WCAG 1.4.11), in the system's accent.

system.$description: The phones' own colours, by reference, never by value: what iOS's UIColor and Material 3's ColorScheme call each, written by scripts/build/design-tokens.sh as that name, so the phone or Material You's wallpaper colours set it at run time, light or dark. The phones' Native look (color.look.native.all) is made of them; the web's Native is shadcn's stock theme (color.look.native.web).

link.$description: What can be tapped: iOS's default tint, Material's primary.

accent.$description: The system's accent, for a mark rather than words: the focus ring.

grouped.$description: A sheet's ground, cards on it.

fill.$description: A muted row or a quiet button's ground.

material.$description: Material 3's container and outline roles, which only Android names; each derived by hand from the look's tint and ground.

wingtip.$description: The Wingtip look's surface containers in Material's steps, lowest to highest, and an outline of 3:1 and more on the sheet (WCAG 1.4.11), so a search bar, a field's edge and an off switch stand off the sheet (the owner's decision, 2026-11-10, on the Android sheet audit's L-1). The sheet is surface-container-low, as Material's bottom sheet is; the search bar surface-container-high, with grey words on it at 4.5:1 and more. At night Material's primary is the night tint #57a8ff, 6:1 on the sheet (L-2), with the navy's words on it.

surface-container-high.$description: The search bar: 1.13:1 off the sheet as Material's own steps are, the muted grey words on it 4.6:1.

surface-container-highest.$description: An off switch's track, inside the outline.

outline.$description: 4.1:1 on the sheet: an off switch's ring, a field's edge.

surface-container-high.$description: The search bar: 1.35:1 off the sheet, the muted words on it 5.5:1.

material-primary.$description: Material's primary at night: the night tint, 6:1 on the sheet, where the web's darker fill is 3:1 (L-2).

sans.$description: The web's text face where no look sets one, and the Native look's: Inter, the face shadcn's vega preset installs (@fontsource-variable/inter, 2026-09-17). The phones use the system's (SF Pro, Roboto).

brand.$description: Both looks' text face on the web.

display.$description: Chart ink's face for a figure's label, an ident and a word button on the web; the phones set the system face's condensed width with letterspaced capitals.

type.$description: The text roles, by what the words are. Sizes in points (CSS px at 1rem = 16px; Android sp) as iOS sets them on a touch screen; the web's mouse size beside. iOS takes the named Dynamic Type style, so each grows with the pilot's text size; Android the named Material type-scale slot, at Material 3's own size for that slot where `android` gives one ({"slot", "fontSize", "lineHeight"}: 16 on 24 for a row, 14 on 20 for prose, 12 on 16 for a note), so the Android app reads as Android rather than as iOS at 17/15/13 (the UI audit, 2026-11-09).

hero.$description: A name over a card's picture: iOS's Title 1, as Maps sets a place's over its photos.

card.$description: A card's name: an airport's, the airspace's, Nearest's (iOS Title 2).

heading.$description: A section's title in the panel's tabs (iOS Title 3), 20 with a mouse too (decision 0021).

title.$description: A drawer's or a sheet's own title, as a navigation bar's (iOS Headline); 16 with a mouse.

row.$description: A row's name and its value, the body (iOS Body); 16 with a mouse, a desktop's body size (it was 14, and the desktop panel read small: the UI audit, 2026-11-09).

prose.$description: What is read rather than scanned: a summary, a paragraph (iOS Subheadline); 16 with a mouse.

detail.$description: The line under a row's name (iOS Subheadline); 14 with a mouse.

note.$description: A section's line of help, a group's heading, a key (iOS Footnote); 13 with a mouse too, the least a desktop's words are.

tab-bar.$description: The tab bar's words (iOS Caption 1, 12/16; the iOS audit's P3).

badge.$description: A StatusBadge's word (Active, Closed, In the air): iOS's Caption 1 in semibold, 12 on 16, the same with a mouse.

caption.$description: A chip's category in a narrow column (iOS Caption 2).

chip.$description: A chip's words over the map (lib/mapChrome CHIP_TEXT): a note's 13 to a finger, 12 with a mouse, and never past 14 px however large the pilot's text, so a chip stays a chip over the chart. The web's alone; the phones' chips are their platform's own.

label.$description: A figure's name, an ident, a chip's word: the display face's capitals, spaced a tenth of an em (letterSpacing in em).

figure.$description: A figure in the strip: 26 on 31, bold, tabular digits (the Flying screen's size). iOS scales it with Title 1.

word.$description: A word button's words: the display face's capitals, spaced 0.08em, at the button's own size.

space.$description: The spacing scale in points, 4 apart (Tailwind's spacing unit, iOS's and Material's 4/8 grid).

hairline.$description: A one-point seam between joined segments, as a timeline's legs.

xxs.$description: Half a step: between a row's name and the line under it, as iOS stacks a title over its subtitle, and a chip's words over and under.

sm.$description: Between rows (gap-2), so 44-point hit areas meet.

lg.$description: The side gutter at phone width.

base.$description: The corners the web's stock components scale from (--radius).

ink.$description: Chart ink's base: a button's 10 and a chip's 7 come from it.

badge.$description: A row's coloured badge and an airspace class's chip, as iOS's Settings rounds its row icons.

control.$description: A large button (48 high) and a menu's panel, as iOS 26 rounds them.

card.$description: Chart ink's card: white, no edge, a soft shade (the canvas's boards).

banner.$description: A banner or a floating bar over the map: half the 44-point tap target, a capsule at one line (the copilot's, the alerts', the weather loop's).

dialog.$description: An alert's corners (the sheets audit's D3); Material's extra-large.

stock.$description: The web's Native look (color.look.native) beyond its colours: shadcn's and Tailwind's own corners, shadows, type and states, as they ship, in place of Wingtip's. scripts/build/design-tokens.sh writes them over the theme on html[data-brand="native"]. The phones' Native takes its platform's own instead (SwiftUI's and Material's defaults), so only the web reads these.

radius.$description: Each of Wingtip's corners as the stock step of shadcn's radius scale (--radius 10, sm 6, md 8, xl 14) a stock component of that kind takes.

control.$description: rounded-md, a stock button's and menu's.

depth.$description: Tailwind's stock shadows: shadow-md for what floats and a menu (a stock popover's), shadow-lg for a sheet, shadow-sm for a card. The map's own marks keep theirs (feel.mark).

material.$description: No frost: a stock popover and drawer are solid.

motion.$description: The Wingtip sheet's own moves (a phone's sheet settling back, the map's buttons riding on it) at shadcn's stock Sheet's time: duration-200, ease-in-out (Tailwind's cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)). The map's panel is Base UI's Drawer, already on its own stock time; the map's camera flights are the chart's, not a sheet's, and keep theirs.

type.$description: Each fixed text role at Tailwind's stock step, with that step's own leading (Tailwind's theme: xs 12/16, sm 14/20, base 16/24, lg 18/28, xl 20/28, 2xl 24/32). The roles that follow the pointer (title, row, prose, detail) are a stock step with a mouse already, and Native has no touch size.

material.$description: What floats over the chart. The web frosts it as Apple's Maps on the web does; iOS uses its system materials (Liquid Glass) and Android Material's tonal surfaces.

glass-blur.$description: The blur behind the map's buttons and the panel's pill (liquid-glass).

glass-fill.$description: How much of the ground is in the glass by day.

glass-fill-dark.$description: And of the popover's colour at night.

bar-blur.$description: The blur behind a bar of controls floating over a card's content (the airport card's tabs), denser than the map buttons' as Apple's floating bars are: over a photo the words read on the frost, not the picture (the owner's C1, 2026-11-14).

bar-fill.$description: How much of the ground is in that bar's glass, by day and at night: 0.92 keeps the unselected labels 4.5:1 or more over a black or a white picture (0.85 at night fell to about 3.5:1 over white).

sheet-blur.$description: The frost behind a sheet's material (backdrop-blur-xl).

motion.$description: The sheet moves as Apple Maps' does: ease-out, no spring, a throw moving one size (the owner, 2026-10-15; docs/decisions/0018).

sheet.$description: Pill to half, in seconds (Maps' measured 0.17 to 0.23 s to 98%).

sheet-most.$description: The longest settle, half to full.

sheet-back-ease.$description: A phone's floating sheet easing back after a drag.

drawer.$description: The web's sheet and cards: Base UI's Drawer on its own demo's time, which what rides it (the map's corner controls, the grabber's capsule) moves on too, so nothing lags or leads it (the motion audit, 2026-11-11).

drawer-ease.$description: Base UI's Drawer's own curve, with its time.

quick.$description: A band's colour under a scrolled head.

page.$description: A card or page giving way to the next one (iOS's navigation transition, Material's shared axis, the web's view transition), on the sheet's ease-out; none with Reduce Motion.

skeleton-pulse.$description: One breath of a skeleton row while its data loads; held still with Reduce Motion.

feel.$description: The web's depth for its own surfaces over the chart: layered shadows a hairline round them. Stock components keep their own states and shadows (the owner, 2026-11-10); iOS and Android take their system's own (Liquid Glass, Material's elevation); only the web reads these.

float.$description: What floats over the chart (the glass buttons, banners, the desktop's panel): a hairline, a contact shade and a soft one.

card.$description: Chart ink's card shade (black at 8%), in place of an edge.

sheet.$description: A sheet's shade, cast up over the chart from its top edge.

hairline.$description: A half-point ring in the look's own --border, in place of a border that would take room: a glance's tile, a watch's row. Its colour is the look's border token, so it follows each look and the night.

mark.$description: A marker's drop shade on the chart (a waypoint's, a numbered stop's, own ship's), the same at night, as the chart under it is.

overlay.$description: A menu, popover, palette or dialog over everything.

haptic.$description: The taps a pilot feels on a key action, one per kind, each platform's own: an iOS sensory feedback, an Android HapticFeedbackConstants name (the API 30 one with its fallback below that), a web navigator.vibrate pattern in milliseconds. None with Reduce Motion, and none where the platform has no vibration.

altitude.$description: An altitude set: a wheel's detent, as a picker ticks.

direct-to.$description: Direct To or Fly Here taken: the route has changed under the pilot.

warning.$description: An alert or a copilot warning shown: felt as well as seen, in a busy cockpit.

detent.$description: The sheet settling at a detent (pill, half, full).

tap-target.$description: The least hit area, in points (Apple's HIG). Controls keep their stock size; a pseudo-element or content shape makes the area (docs/decisions/0030).

chip.$description: A chip's height; its hit area is the tap target round it.

map-button.$description: A button of the map's own capsule (Map, My Position, Ask), one piece of glass as Apple Maps' 48-point buttons are (the owner's decision, 2026-11-10).

tab-bar.$description: What the iOS 26 floating tab bar covers at a sheet's foot over the home indicator's inset: the sheet's content is padded by it so its main actions are not under the bar (the UI audit, 2026-11-09, item 2).

panel.$description: The map panel's width beside the map, from a tablet's width (768) up: a card at the left.

panel-wide.$description: The map panel's width on a desktop, from 1024 wide: a side panel with room for a desktop's type (the UI audit, 2026-11-09).

desktop.$description: The window width from which the web is laid out for a desktop: the wide side panel, the mouse's hover and the keyboard's shortcuts (Tailwind's lg).

refresh-pull.$description: How far a live list (a field's weather, the Brief, traffic) is pulled down before letting go refreshes it, as iOS's refresh control.

map.$description: The map's camera and the zooms its marks change at, one number each for every app (the web's zoom is MapLibre's plus one, glZoom). The 3D view's pitches are degrees.

pitch-open.$description: The tilt 3D opens at, for the ground to read as ground at once.

pitch-max.$description: As far as the map tilts in 3D.

pitch-flat-max.$description: MapLibre's own most, as the map is made (the flat map keeps it).

zoom-station-close.$description: The station model (barb and its two lines) is drawn from this zoom in.

zoom-station-always.$description: The station model's zoom with the look Station, at every zoom it fits.

zoom-barb-far-from.$description: Farther out the barb the wind earns is drawn from this zoom, none past a region's scale.

zoom-barb-full.$description: The far barb is full size from this zoom, 0.6 of it at zoom-barb-far-from.

zoom-world-wind.$description: At this zoom and out the GFS's world wind streaks run past AWC's box.

zoom-streak-near.$description: At this zoom and closer the wind streaks have their shortest life; each zoom out lengthens it.

airspace-shade-mix.$description: How far a 3D airspace volume's ink is mixed toward color.chart.airspace-floor-low at a surface floor and toward airspace-floor-high at airspace-shade-top-ft and over, 0 to 1.

airspace-shade-top-ft.$description: The floor, feet MSL, at which a 3D volume is shaded lightest: a Class B's top, as Chicago's (a drawing scale, not a rule).

airspace-faded.$description: How strongly a 3D airspace volume not at the plan's altitudes is drawn, times its own opacity.

airspace-held.$description: And one at the plan's altitudes, times its own opacity.

airspace-label-faded.$description: How strongly a 3D shelf's altitudes are written where the plan is not at it: fainter, still legible.

flow.$description: Model Weather's colour scales: a ramp is its stops, low to high, each [value in the field's unit, the colour's name in color.weather, opacity in 255ths]; an alpha is the opacities of a field whose values the engine's bands give (model_weather_bands, aviation_grid_bands), in band order; a cover is how strongly a field covers the chart, 0 to 1 (features/weather-flow).

ramp-wind.$description: The wind's and the gusts' field, knots.

ramp-streak.$description: The wind streaks, fainter where the wind is light, knots.

ramp-temp.$description: Temperature, degrees C, to -60 so the flight levels' cold is told apart, held at the hot end to 45.

alpha-rain.$description: Precipitation: clear under the least reflectivity, then at it, at moderate, heavy, extreme and the strongest returns.

alpha-ceiling.$description: The ceiling's categories, LIFR to VFR, strongest lowest.

alpha-cape.$description: CAPE: none, half the moderate floor, then moderate, strong and extreme.

alpha-icing.$description: AWC's icing categories, each a whole step.

cover-tint.$description: A light tint, as the chart under the wind and its gusts still has to be read.

cover-wash.$description: The default cover, and the freezing level's and the cloud tops'.

cover-solid.$description: Nearly solid, as Apple Weather's temperature map is, and the precipitation where it falls.

scale-wind-ticks.$description: The wind's and the gusts' legend ticks, knots: the wind ramp's stops.

scale-rain-headroom.$description: How far past extreme's least reflectivity (the engine's model_weather_bands) the precipitation's ramp reaches its strongest colour, dBZ: where the brightest returns are, short of the picture's 75 dBZ top.

format.$description: How Wingtip writes a figure, as examples: each value is a list of [input, written] pairs. The generator writes them to apps/web/src/lib/fixtures/formats.json, the table each app's one formatter is tested against (the web's lib/format; the phones' later), so a figure reads the same on every screen and every app. The spoken- forms are what a screen reader says for the written ones (an accessibility label): the same figure in full words. Inputs are a number (feet, minutes, degrees, knots, nautical miles, gallons, pounds), null for no figure, a list for a range, or an ISO time.

cruise-altitude.$description: A cruising altitude on the cruise controls, the profile and the route box: FL and three figures of hundreds of feet, against FAA usage on purpose (docs/decisions/0009; the owner, 2026-10-27).

map-level.$description: An altitude on the map's weather (AIRMETs, SIGMETs, PIREPs): FL and three figures, no dash (docs/decisions/0009; the owner, 2026-11-06).

altitude.$description: Any other altitude, height or elevation: grouped feet, as the FAA writes them. An em dash for no figure, which is not zero.

altitude-range.$description: The altitudes a route flies, lowest to highest.

duration.$description: A time aloft, a time left or an age: Intl.DurationFormat's narrow style (the owner, 2026-10-28).

nav-log-time.$description: A leg's time en route as a paper nav log writes it.

zulu.$description: A UTC clock time as reports and flight plans give it.

heading.$description: A course, heading, track or wind direction: three figures, whole degrees, north as 360 (FAA Order JO 7110.65, 2-4-17).

distance.$description: Nautical miles to a tenth, as the planner sends them.

speed.$description: An airspeed, a ground speed or a wind speed: whole knots.

fuel.$description: Fuel in US gallons to a tenth.

wind-correction.$description: A wind correction angle: plus to the right, a minus sign to the left.

variation.$description: Magnetic variation as the sectional's isogonic lines write it (FAA-H-8083-25C, chapter 16).

$value: one two thousand five hundred feet
one thousand two hundred thirty-four feet
spoken-altitude.$description: An altitude as VoiceOver, TalkBack and a screen reader say it (the accessibility label of a written altitude or cruising altitude): the separate digits of the thousands, then the hundreds, as a pilot hears it from ATC (AIM 4-2-9a), and what is left in words. A screen reader is not a radio, so nine is "nine", not the radio's "niner" (AIM 4-2-8).

spoken-heading.$description: A course, heading, track or wind direction said: its three figures one by one (AIM 4-2-10), north as three six zero, as the written form (FAA Order JO 7110.65, 2-4-17).

spoken-heading-magnetic.$description: A magnetic course or heading said, with its reference: the nav log's magnetic course and heading.

spoken-heading-true.$description: A true course or heading said, with "true" added as AIM 4-2-10 asks wherever a direction is not magnetic.

$value: one hundred two point four nautical miles
spoken-distance.$description: A distance said in words, to the written tenth, a whole number with no "point zero".

spoken-speed.$description: An airspeed, ground speed or wind speed said in words, whole knots as written.

spoken-fuel.$description: Fuel said in words, US gallons to the written tenth.

spoken-duration.$description: A time aloft, a time left or an age said in full words, rounded to the minute as written.

spoken-zulu.$description: A UTC time said digit by digit and "zulu", as the AIM gives a time (AIM 4-2-13), nine as "nine".
